general_information.Description: University Success Oral Communication is designed for English language learners preparing for mainstream academic environments. A flexible three-part approach includes intensive and systematic skill development tied to learning outcomes along with authentic lectures delivered by top professors from Stanford University. The Oral Communication strand provides real-life learning experiences for students who need to achieve academic autonomy. Upon completion of the course, students should be able to: LO1. Listening actively to follow a lecture or discussion, taking organized notes and identifying subject relative clause LO2. Demonstrating an understanding of ideas in a discussion, answering questions about texts, and using tag questions to invite agreement LO3. Formulating probing questions, describing conclusions, summarising listening, and connecting ideas with so and therefore LO4. Comparing similar ideas and contrasting different ideas, understanding relationships between ideas, and utilizing the simple past passive LO5. Identifying parts of a presentation or lecture, planning for a presentation, making predictions, explaining order with linking words LO6. Identifying and expressing facts, and opinions, bias, expressing conditions with if LO7. Making inferences, giving oral summaries to relate ideas, answering inference questions, and expressing present possibility with modal verbs LO8. Taking note on research lectures, relating source information to an audience, synthesizing information from multiple sources, and using compliment clauses after about LO9. Identifying main ideas, paraphrasing to relate main ideas, rephrasing to simplify ideas, and constructing the present perfect passive LO10. Interpreting an listing steps in a process, utilizing visual aids in a presentation, explaining a scientific process, and showing sequence with time adverbs LO11. Contributing interesting ideas to make classroom atmosphere more exciting. LO12. Budgeting your time wisely and performing certain independent learning. LO13. Supporting students with poor academic performance in pair-work/group-work activities.
general_information.StudentTasks: - Attend at least 80% of contact hours in order to be accepted to the final examination - Actively participate in class activities - Fulfil tasks given by the instructor after class - Use their own laptop in class only for learning purposes - Use the Student Access Code provided with the textbook - Access the course website for up-to-date information and material of the course, for online support from teachers and other students, and for practicing and assessment.
general_information.Tools: Tools: Foxit pdf editor Internet access
general_information.Note: 1) On-going assessment: 50% - Progress test: 03*10% - Assignment: 02*10% 2) Final Examination (FE) 50% 3) Final Result 100%

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ1
constructive_questions.Details: What do you know about endangered species? Illustrate with the general statistics of the past and present.

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ2
constructive_questions.Details: Should people be concerned about endangered species? Why or why not? Provide justification.

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ3
constructive_questions.Details: Research an endangered species in Vietnam. What are some reasons leading to this? What should be done to protect the species?

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ4
constructive_questions.Details: Research an endangered species in Australia or a country of your choice. What are causes? Has the Governement been making any attempts in protecting this species?

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ5
constructive_questions.Details: What is a hybrid animal? How is it created? Compare and contrast with a normal one. Are there any real-life examples?

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ6
constructive_questions.Details: What health problems may a hybrid animal face? Illustrate with visualizations and examples. Make some suggestions if possible.

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ7
constructive_questions.Details: What is de-extinction? What are the pros when scientists and conservationists decide to apply this practice?

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ8
constructive_questions.Details: What are the disadvantages of de-extinction? Are there any possible solutions?

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ9
constructive_questions.Details: How important is customer feedback to a company when it is developing a product? Explain your answer and give an example.

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ10
constructive_questions.Details: Discuss some ways that can be used to get customer feedback. Illustrate with real-world cases.

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ11
constructive_questions.Details: Examine a well-designed product. Describe the item. Why, in your opinion, is it designed well?

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ12
constructive_questions.Details: Examine a well-designed product. Describe the item. What, in your opinion, can be done to make the design even better?

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ13
constructive_questions.Details: What types of products or items do young people consider useful but older individuals may not? Why would that be the case?Is there anything that can be done to change someone's opinion for the better?

constructive_questions.Details: Discuss different ways product desingers source inspiration and devise new ideas.

constructive_questions.Details: Numerous new products are being designed and manufactured in the present day. Do you consider it important to do so? Why or why not?

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ16
constructive_questions.Details: Discuss mobile-first design. How is it applied in real-world cases?
